blocks.text: 当你的代码要从模型回复里读取字段，比如订单号或退款金额时，它期望每次都能拿到干净的 JSON。大多数时候确实如此。但偶尔模型会把 JSON 包在代码围栏里，或者多塞一个你没要求的字段，或者把数字当成文本来发，你的代码就崩了。如果你同时用多个模型，一套修复方案覆盖不了全部，因为每个模型和提供商处理结构化输出的方式都不一样。

inlines.text: 当你的代码要从模型回复里读取字段，比如订单号或退款金额时，它期望每次都能拿到干净的 JSON。大多数时候确实如此。但偶尔模型会把 JSON 包在代码围栏里，或者多塞一个你没要求的字段，或者把数字当成文本来发，你的代码就崩了。如果你同时用多个模型，一套修复方案覆盖不了全部，因为每个模型和提供商处理结构化输出的方式都不一样。

blocks.text: 要拿到可靠的 LLM 结构化输出有三种办法，选哪种取决于模型支持什么。如果它支持结构化输出，就给它发严格的 JSON Schema。如果它只支持工具，就让它调用一个使用你 schema 的工具。如果你只需要一个标签，比如“退款”或“换货”，那就改用决策模型。在 OpenRouter 上，这三种方式共用同一个 API key 和同一种请求格式。

blocks.text: 为了看每种方式效果如何，我们用 24 条杂乱的支持工单消息，在九个支持结构化输出的模型上做了测试，另外还加了一个只支持工具的 GLM 5.3 FlashX。这九个模型共 216 条回复中有 209 条符合严格 schema，7 条失败全部来自同一个无视 schema 的提供商。而当我们只在提示词里要求输出 JSON 时，有 18 条回复失败，每次都是因为代码围栏。

blocks.text: TL;DR

inlines.text: TL;DR
在 response_format 里发送严格 schema，并设置 require_parameters: true，这样当没有端点支持时请求会直接失败。
如果模型只有工具，就把 schema 放进一个工具里并强制调用。
对损坏的 JSON 保持开启 Response Healing，同时自己校验每一条回复。有些端点接受了严格 schema，照样会把它弄坏。
如果你只需要一个标签，像 Jev 这样的决策模型会返回各个选项上的概率，根本没有东西需要解析。

blocks.text: 第 1 步：写一个所有提供商都能接受的 schema

inlines.text: 第 1 步：写一个所有提供商都能接受的 schema

blocks.text: 当提供商有严格模式时，模型只能写出让输出符合你 schema 的文本。这就是严格模式输出里不会出现代码围栏和多余文字的原因。

inlines.text: 当提供商有严格模式时，模型只能写出让输出符合你 schema 的文本。这就是严格模式输出里不会出现代码围栏和多余文字的原因。

blocks.text: 要做到这一点，OpenAI 的严格模式需要提前知道每一个键。每个属性都必须列在 required 里，每个对象都必须设置 additionalProperties: false。如果某个值可能缺失，你要在它的类型里加上 null，而不是把这个键省掉。

inlines.text: 要做到这一点，OpenAI 的严格模式需要提前知道每一个键。每个属性都必须列在 required 里，每个对象都必须设置 additionalProperties: false。如果某个值可能缺失，你要在它的类型里加上 null，而不是把这个键省掉。

blocks.text: 这些是我们找到的最严格的规则，遵循它们的 schema 在我们试过的每个模型上都能用。当我们加了一个可选的 note 字段时，GPT-6 Luna 用这个错误拒绝了请求。

blocks.text: 第 2 步：发送 schema，或者强制一次工具调用

inlines.text: 第 2 步：发送 schema，或者强制一次工具调用

blocks.text: 同一个 schema 可以用两种方式交给模型。放在 response_format 里，它控制消息文本；作为工具的参数，它控制工具调用的参数，而支持严格工具调用的提供商在那里也施加同样的限制。所以如果你强制模型调用那一个工具并保留它的参数，你就能从一个有工具但没有结构化输出的模型那里拿到结构化输出。你的代码永远不会真正运行这个工具。

blocks.text: 结构化输出的支持是按端点划分的，也就是按提供该模型的服务商划分，而不是按模型本身划分。结构化输出文档也是这么说的。2026 年 10 月 8 日，我们模型 API 中的 469 个模型 ID 里有 386 个在 supported_parameters 中列出了 structured_outputs，401 个列出了 tools，还有 55 个有 tools 但没有结构化输出。

blocks.text: 这个插件有几个限制，你应该了解一下。

inlines.text: 这个插件有几个限制，你应该了解一下。
它只在请求把 response_format 设为 json_schema 或 json_object 时运行。它正是靠这一点判断回复应该是 JSON。当我们只把 schema 放在提示词里时，代码围栏原样返回，没有被处理。
它只对非流式请求有效。
它不会处理工具调用的参数。
它无法修复被 max_tokens 截断的回复。这就是脚本要先检查 finish_reason 是否为“length”的原因。

blocks.text: When your code reads fields from a model’s reply, like an order ID or a refund amount, it expects clean JSON every time. Most of the time, it gets it. But now and then the model wraps the JSON in a code fence, adds a field you didn’t ask for, or sends a number as text, and your code breaks. If you use several models, one fix won’t cover them all, because each model and provider handles structured output in its own way.

inlines.text: When your code reads fields from a model’s reply, like an order ID or a refund amount, it expects clean JSON every time. Most of the time, it gets it. But now and then the model wraps the JSON in a code fence, adds a field you didn’t ask for, or sends a number as text, and your code breaks. If you use several models, one fix won’t cover them all, because each model and provider handles structured output in its own way.

blocks.text: There are three ways to get reliable LLM structured output, and the right one depends on what the model supports. If it supports structured outputs, send it a strict JSON Schema. If it only supports tools, make it call a tool that uses your schema. And if you only need a label, like “refund” or “exchange,” use a decision model instead. On OpenRouter, all three work with one API key and one request format.

inlines.text: There are three ways to get reliable LLM structured output, and the right one depends on what the model supports. If it
supports structured

outputs, send it a strict JSON Schema. If it only supports tools, make it call a tool that uses your schema. And if you only need a label, like “refund” or “exchange,” use a decision model instead. On OpenRouter, all three work with one API key and one request format.

blocks.text: To see how well each way works, we tested them with 24 messy support messages on nine models that support structured outputs, plus GLM 5.3 FlashX, which only supports tools. Across the nine, 209 of 216 replies matched a strict schema, and all 7 misses came from one provider that ignores the schema. When we only asked for JSON in the prompt, 18 replies failed, each time because of a code fence.

blocks.text: TL;DR

inlines.text: TL;DR
Send a strict schema in response_format and set require_parameters: true, so the request fails when no endpoint supports it.
If the model only has tools, put the schema in one tool and force the call.
Keep Response Healing on for broken JSON, and validate every reply yourself. Some endpoints accept a strict schema and still break it.
If you only need a label, a decision model such as Jev returns probabilities over your options, so there’s nothing to parse.

blocks.text: Step 1: Write a schema every provider accepts

inlines.text: Step 1: Write a schema every provider accepts

blocks.text: When a provider has a strict mode, the model can only write text that keeps the output valid against your schema. That’s why code fences and extra text don’t show up in strict-mode output.

inlines.text: When a provider has a strict mode, the model can only write text that keeps the output valid against your schema. That’s why code fences and extra text don’t show up in strict-mode output.

blocks.text: To do this, OpenAI’s strict mode needs to know every key ahead of time. Every property must be listed in required, and every object must set additionalProperties: false. If a value can be missing, you add null to its type instead of leaving the key out.

inlines.text: To do this, OpenAI’s strict mode needs to know every key ahead of time. Every property must be listed in required, and every object must set additionalProperties: false. If a value can be missing, you add null to its type instead of leaving the key out.

blocks.text: These were the strictest rules we found, and a schema that follows them worked on every model we tried. When we added an optional note field, GPT-6 Luna rejected the request with this error.

blocks.text: You can give the same schema to a model in two ways. In response_format, it controls the message text. As the parameters of a tool, it controls the tool call’s arguments, and providers with strict tool calling apply the same limits there. So if you force the model to call that one tool and keep its arguments, you get structured output from a model that has tools but no structured outputs. Your code never runs the tool.

blocks.text: The extra input didn’t decide the cost, though. Most models wrote fewer tokens when they answered through a tool, so the forced tool call was cheaper on six of the nine models. How much a model writes changes from run to run, so check the cost on your own requests.

inlines.text: Step 5: Keep Response Healing on for syntax errors

blocks.text: The Response Healing plugin fixes LLM JSON output after the model finishes. It removes code fences and fixes broken JSON, such as a missing bracket or a trailing comma. It doesn’t read your schema.

inlines.text: The
Response Healing plugin
fixes LLM JSON output after the model finishes. It removes code fences and fixes broken JSON, such as a missing bracket or a trailing comma. It doesn’t read your schema.

blocks.text: On GLM, it took json_schema from 0 valid outputs to 19 of 24, and all 24 replies parsed as JSON. The other five still had a field the schema doesn’t allow. Only a provider that enforces the schema, or your own validator, catches that.

inlines.text: On GLM, it took json_schema from 0 valid outputs to 19 of 24, and all 24 replies parsed as JSON. The other five still had a field the schema doesn’t allow. Only a provider that enforces the schema, or your own validator, catches that.

blocks.text: The plugin has a few limits you should know about.

inlines.text: The plugin has a few limits you should know about.

It only runs when the request sets response_format to json_schema or json_object. That’s how it knows the reply should be JSON. When we put the schema only in the prompt, the code fences came back untouched.
It only works on requests that aren’t streamed.
It doesn’t touch tool call arguments.
It can’t fix a reply that max_tokens cut off. That’s why the script checks finish_reason for “length” first.

blocks.text: On models that enforce the schema, it had nothing to fix, so there’s no reason to turn it off.

blocks.text: When the output is a label, use a decision model

inlines.text: When the output is a label, use a decision model

blocks.text: Some fields, like intent and needs_human, are decisions. One is a pick from a fixed list, and the other is a yes or no. A chat model writes these answers as text, which is why they need a schema and a validator.

inlines.text: Some fields, like intent and needs_human, are decisions. One is a pick from a fixed list, and the other is a yes or no. A chat model writes these answers as text, which is why they need a schema and a validator.

blocks.text: A decision model such as Jev doesn’t write anything. It scores the options you list and returns a probability for each one, using your own keys, so its answer can’t come back in the wrong shape. You call it through the Decisions API, with the input as state and a short description of each option in criteria.

blocks.text: Frequently asked questions

inlines.text: Frequently asked questions

blocks.text: What does structured JSON output mean?

inlines.text: What does structured JSON output mean?

blocks.text: It means the model returns JSON with the same keys and value types every time, so your code can read the fields directly.

inlines.text: It means the model returns JSON with the same keys and value types every time, so your code can read the fields directly.

blocks.text: Is JSON mode the same as structured outputs?

inlines.text: Is JSON mode the same as structured outputs?

blocks.text: No. JSON mode (“type”: “json_object”) only promises valid JSON. Structured outputs (“type”: “json_schema”) send your schema, and providers with a strict mode make the output follow it.

inlines.text: No. JSON mode (“type”: “json_object”) only promises valid JSON. Structured outputs (“type”: “json_schema”) send your schema, and providers with a strict mode make the output follow it.

blocks.text: Does strict mode guarantee schema-valid output?

inlines.text: Does strict mode guarantee schema-valid output?

blocks.text: Only where the provider enforces it. Some providers treat the schema as a strong hint, and in our test one endpoint ignored strict: true on 7 of 24 requests.

inlines.text: Only where the provider enforces it. Some providers treat the schema as a strong hint, and in our test one endpoint ignored strict: true on 7 of 24 requests.

blocks.text: What is the difference between function calling and structured outputs?

inlines.text: What is the difference between function calling and structured outputs?

blocks.text: Structured outputs apply your schema to the message text. Function calling, also called tool calling, applies it to a tool call’s arguments.

inlines.text: Structured outputs apply your schema to the message text. Function calling, also called tool calling, applies it to a tool call’s arguments.

blocks.text: Can you stream structured output?

inlines.text: Can you stream structured output?

blocks.text: Yes. Add stream: true to a json_schema request. Response Healing doesn’t run on streamed requests, so validate the full reply when the stream ends.

blocks.text: How do I get structured output from a model that does not support it?

blocks.text: If the model has tools, force one tool call with your schema as its parameters. If not, use JSON mode with the schema in the prompt, Response Healing, and your own validator.
